lines: Take {gift_item}. Better to carry thanks before you need steel.
Here, {gift_item}. I trust you to use it with a cooler head than most.
Good. {gift_item} struck true with {tested_villager}.
Then the advice kept its edge. {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}.
That blade was poorly balanced. For {gift_subject}, try {alternative_gift}.
{gift_item} missed clean? Bring {alternative_gift}; better weight for the hand.

messages.text: That advice had a dull edge. Try {alternative_gift}; it should bite better.
You swung with what I handed you. Next time, choose {alternative_gift}.

openings.text: Mind the grindstone. What do you need?

closings.text: Back to keeping blades honest, then.

pacify.text: Fine. I will let the blade rest, but do not test me again.
No. Some threats do not get to buy their way closer.

lines: Rust on a sword is just neglect learning to speak.
Trouble always finds villages. Best be ready.
A blade tells the truth about its owner sooner or later.
Ready is not the same as eager. A village should know the difference.
Keeping an edge honest is mostly knowing when to stop grinding.
An unready guard is just confidence standing in the wrong place.
The golem did good work last night. Still, I keep the blades sharp.
I once polished rust off a sword and found three old mistakes underneath.
Some nights, the grindstone sounds like preparation instead of work.

lines.text: Mind the grindstone. It has no patience for wandering fingers.
Weapon jokes are sharp. I keep the dull ones for people who lean too close.
That was dull enough to be safe, at least.
Stand back. I know the sound trouble makes when it wants to be casual.

lines: I remember fighting something inside me and losing. You gave me another weapon: morning.
The cure struck true. I remember you standing on the right side of it.
Your face rings like steel, but the battle around it is smoke.
I remember wanting to bite, then wanting to breathe. You were there between them.

lines.text: I remember you, and I remember being dangerous. Do not make me relive either too quickly.

lines: Thunder shook the grindstone so hard the blades rang before anyone touched them, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked blades, axes, and watch posts after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
Near the grindstone, the bell sounded small under that thunder. We stayed inside and kept the doors watched.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked the weapon racks twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have weapon racks to set right.
I checked coal, handles, and weapon racks for sparks first, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I checked the coal and handles after.
The grindstone can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could reach around the grindstone, then stopped pretending things matter more than neighbors.
The smoke is thinning near the grindstone, but everyone is still sniffing the air like it might lie.
During a raid, the grindstone can wait; who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but my hands near the grindstone still expect another wave from the road.
We counted living neighbors before blades, axes, and watch posts. That is the only count worth starting with.
Raiders came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the grindstone and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the grindstone, I saw fear cross the square; then I saw courage get there first.
Night trouble tests the loose latch by the grindstone first. We are fixing those before sunset.
I stayed near the watch post past the torchlight and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn gave the grindstone enough light to count wounds, missing blocks, and who made it home.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping a sharpened edge between us and teeth.
We are safe enough near the grindstone, though every shadow is being inspected twice.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning grit from the edges.
I checked blades, axes, and watch posts, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.
Sand reached the grindstone, the hinges, and half our eyes, but no one has been reported missing.
A hard wind teaches a weaponsmith which doors actually close and which ones only pretend.
We are safe enough near the grindstone, though the whole village sounds like it is chewing gravel.
The grindstone can wait. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the doors, but everyone near the grindstone found shelter.
Cold works quietly around the grindstone. We are checking on anyone who stayed quiet too long.
I am clearing ice off the axe heads and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
We are alright for now near the grindstone. Keep the fires fed and the paths open.
